facts.raw_span: continuous chest pain for two hours
denied dyspnea, syncope, or prior similar episodes
no personal or family history of cardiovascular or thromboembolic disease
sinus rhythm with 2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3
right ventricular dilatation and an estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg
continuous chest pain for two hours
denied dyspnea, syncope, or prior similar episodes
no personal or family history of cardiovascular or thromboembolic disease
sinus rhythm with 2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3
right ventricular dilatation and an estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg

concepts.why: The patient presented with continuous chest pain and ST-segment elevation, which are characteristic of acute coronary syndrome.
The patient had ST-segment elevation and was given aspirin, clopidogrel, and intravenous heparin, which are typical treatments for myocardial infarction.
The patient developed a new right bundle branch block and had right ventricular dilatation, which are consistent with right ventricular infarction.
The patient had hypoxia and pulmonary hypertension, which are characteristic of pulmonary embolism.
The patient had right ventricular dilatation and a new right bundle branch block, which are consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
The patient had pulmonary hypertension without any obvious cause, which is consistent with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension.
The patient had right ventricular dilatation and a new right bundle branch block, which are consistent with cardiac sarcoidosis.
The patient had right ventricular dilatation and ST-segment elevation, which are consistent with stress-induced cardiomyopathy.

rationales.F01: Chest pain is a common symptom of acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: ST-segment elevation is a hallmark of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: New right bundle branch block is consistent with right ventricular infarction.
rationales.F11: Normal coronary arteries without stenosis rule out acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F12: Right ventricular dilatation and elevated pulmonary arterial pressure are consistent with right ventricular infarction and pulmonary embolism.

frontier_selector.rationale: new right bundle branch block and right ventricular dilatation with elevated pulmonary arterial pressure, despite normal coronary arteries
